originalTitle: US stock: S&P 500 ends lower as investors weigh data, Middle East tensions
simplifiedContent: The US stock market, measured by the S&P 500, went down because investors are worried about some not-so-great news about how much people are spending money. This is important because when people spend less, it can be a sign that the economy is slowing down. Some stocks, like Applied Materials, did poorly, which also hurt other similar stocks related to artificial intelligence. On the other hand, oil companies did well because oil prices are going up, and Reddit's stock surged after it was added to an important list. This mix of good and bad news caused the market to end the day lower.

originalTitle: Nvidia’s $500 billion plan envelops Wall Street in its AI frenzy
simplifiedContent: Nvidia, a big tech company, has announced a huge $500 billion plan to help companies that make artificial intelligence (AI) chips. They're working with big banks to offer loans to these companies, which are often small startups. This plan is important because many companies need powerful computers to develop AI, and Nvidia wants to help them get the money they need. By doing this, Nvidia is trying to support the growth of the tech industry and help build the infrastructure needed for AI. This could be a big deal for the tech industry and the companies involved in AI development.

originalTitle: How a $900 million bet on SpaceX turned 100x into $94 billion for Alphabet
simplifiedContent: Alphabet, the company that owns Google, invested $900 million in SpaceX, a rocket company, and now that investment is worth about $94 billion. This is a huge return on their investment, meaning they made a lot of money from it. As a result, Alphabet now owns the largest share of SpaceX among institutional investors, which are large organizations that invest money. This matters because it shows how successful Alphabet's investment in SpaceX was, and other early investors like Fidelity and Saudi Arabia also have significant stakes in the company. Alphabet's large ownership stake in SpaceX gives them a significant interest in the company's future success.

originalTitle: Oil Rises as US Warns of More Economic Pressure to Isolate Iran
simplifiedContent: The price of oil has gone up a little bit because the US is thinking about putting more economic pressure on Iran. This means the US might impose new rules or penalties that could hurt Iran's economy. The Strait of Hormuz, a very important route for oil ships, has been affected by a war that's been going on for six months. This warning from the US is making traders (people who buy and sell oil) a bit nervous, which is why the price of oil is rising. This matters because higher oil prices can affect many parts of the economy, including the cost of gasoline and other goods.

originalTitle: Dollar falls on surprise drop in US retail sales
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar has decreased because of an unexpected decrease in the amount of money people spent shopping in the US. This decrease in shopping, also known as retail sales, was a surprise to many people. As a result, the dollar is now worth less compared to other currencies. This change in the dollar's value is important because it can affect the global economy and the stock market. The drop in retail sales and the dollar's decrease in value may influence investment decisions and the overall economic outlook.

originalTitle: Patanjali Foods shares to be in focus on Monday as Q1 net profit jumps 86%; revenue hits record
simplifiedContent: Patanjali Foods, a company listed on the stock market, just released its financial results for the quarter ending June. The company's net profit (or total earnings) increased by 86% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹335.73 crore. The company also made a record amount of revenue, which is the total amount of money it earned from sales, of ₹11,337.45 crore. This news might make investors pay attention to Patanjali Foods' stock on Monday. The company has also decided to give its shareholders a 40% dividend, which means they will receive a portion of the company's profits.
